Field notes from the Tern Island survey.

The ringing crew arrived on the island on the third of May and counted 412 arctic tern nests along the northern shingle. Nest density was highest near the old lighthouse, where the gravel is coarse and the wind keeps the grass short.

Rangers recorded a kestrel hunting over the dunes at dawn. The kestrel took two chicks from the eastern colony before the wardens scared it off with a kite.

Equipment checklist: spotting scope, leg rings (size C), calipers, waterproof notebook, and the spare battery for the GPS logger. The logger is set to fix a position every ten minutes.

Boat transfers run twice daily. The morning boat leaves the harbour at 07:30 and the afternoon boat returns at 16:45. Weather cancellations are announced by the harbour master before 06:00.
